hook: Stop mixing up bored and boring
why: Bored is how you feel. Boring is what makes you feel it.
aha: Tired and tiring work the same way!
ex: I'm bored, so let's go out.

hook: Stop mixing up say and tell
why: Tell needs a person after it. Say does not.
aha: You tell someone, but you say something!

gen.note: real learner confusable pair (Cambridge Dictionary usage notes, Swan Practical English Usage)

hook: Stop mixing up make and do
wrong: I need to make my homework.
right: I need to do my homework.
why: Use do for tasks and jobs. Use make when you create something.
aha: You do the dishes, but you make dinner!
ex: I do my homework after dinner.

gen.note: real learner confusable pair (Cambridge Dictionary usage notes, Swan Practical English Usage)

hook: Stop mixing up fun and funny
why: Fun means you enjoy it. Funny makes you laugh.
aha: Use funny for jokes and comedians!
ex: We had fun at the beach.

quiz.q: We had a lot of ___ at the party.

hook: Stop mixing up affect and effect
why: Affect is the verb. Effect is the noun, the result.
aha: Think A for action, E for end result!

hook: Stop mixing up miss and lose
why: You miss a bus, a train or a class. You lose things, like keys.
aha: You can also miss a person you love!
memory: MISS the bus, LOSE your keys

gen.note: real learner confusable pair (Cambridge Dictionary usage notes, Swan Practical English Usage)

hook: Stop mixing up listen and hear
why: Listen means you try to hear. Hearing just happens.
aha: Listen takes to before the thing you hear!

gen.note: real learner confusable pair (Cambridge Dictionary usage notes, Swan Practical English Usage)

hook: Stop mixing up remind and remember
wrong: Please remember me about the meeting.
right: Please remind me about the meeting.
why: Remind means you help someone remember.
aha: First you remind me, then I remember!

hook: Stop mixing up steal and rob
why: You steal a thing. You rob a person or a place.
aha: Robbers rob banks, and thieves steal money!
memory: STEAL things, ROB people and places
